- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes — if price spiked recently, reduce forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early downward turns; adjust by adding 1–2 days of downward bias if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or negative), model tends to underperform; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to compensate for low sentiment drag.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out — no correction needed unless price deviates >1.5% from recent trend.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong directional shift (e.g., 0.67+ for >3 days); otherwise, apply smoothing to prevent false peaks.
